explainedBy: The reader wakes to a leak and an overdrawn account: two real disasters shown as the water icon over a frightened person.

storyboard.claim: Real problems like a ceiling leak or an overdrawn account seem to demand focus.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The reader in the kitchen, afraid, with water pouring in beside him.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Opens the objection: the hosts leave the theory for a concrete crisis.
storyboard.addedInformation: Gives the objection a physical emergency instead of an abstract worry.

explainedBy: The same kitchen stays; the reader argues he must stare at the problem to solve it.

storyboard.claim: He says he must intensely focus on the disaster to orchestrate a fix.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The same reader, still under the leak, now arguing his case.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same stage; his face moves from fear to insistence.
storyboard.addedInformation: Turns the leak into his argument that focus on a negative is necessary.

explainedBy: The asker presses the objection while the explainer listens: one side pushes, the other receives it.

storyboard.claim: You cannot ignore a flooded kitchen; this is the most common roadblock to the material.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Host A pressing her point, Host B listening across from her.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Back from the kitchen to the two hosts.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the objection as the one everybody hits.

explainedBy: Cause to effect: forceful attention on a problem invites the problem deeper instead of fixing it.

storyboard.claim: Abraham argues forceful attention on a problem invites it deeper rather than fixing it.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A two-step flow from FORCEFUL FOCUS to PROBLEM DEEPER.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The hosts answer the objection with a cause and effect.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the book is claiming attention makes the problem grow.

explainedBy: The book does not say ignore the leak: the reader picks up the phone to call a plumber.

storyboard.claim: They are not saying ignore the leak; you call a plumber.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The reader in the kitchen holding a phone, the leak beside him.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Back to the kitchen to show the sensible action.
storyboard.addedInformation: Separates acting on the problem from obsessing over it.

explainedBy: Staring at the leak in paralysis instead of acting: the same kitchen, his posture now collapsed.

storyboard.claim: Standing there obsessing over damage and cost makes disaster your point of attraction.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The reader slumped and frozen, still holding the phone, staring at the leak.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same stage; he stops acting and just stares.
storyboard.addedInformation: Contrasts the plumber call with paralysed obsessing.

explainedBy: The explainer gives the book's rule: look at the problem only long enough to define the wanted solution, a safe dry house.

storyboard.claim: Look at the problem only long enough to define the solution you want: a dry safe house.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Host B explaining beside a house icon while Host A realizes.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the leak to the solution the text wants you to picture.
storyboard.addedInformation: Gives the wanted solution a concrete image: the house.

explainedBy: After defining the solution, you tune your feeling to its relief; staring at the problem amplifies it.

storyboard.claim: Tune your emotional dial to the relief of the solution; forceful focus amplifies the problem.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Both hosts calm and smiling as the relief is described.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Continues the explanation in the same room.
storyboard.addedInformation: Adds the second step: feel the relief, not the problem.

explainedBy: The core thesis as a chain: attention sets the feeling and the feeling sets what you notice next.

storyboard.claim: Attention dictates what I feel and what I feel dictates what I notice next.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A three-step flow from ATTENTION to WHAT I FEEL to WHAT I NOTICE.
storyboard.onScreenText: ATTENTION -> WHAT I FEEL -> WHAT I NOTICE
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Summarizes the previous beats as one chain.
storyboard.addedInformation: Ties the leak example back to the core thesis.

explainedBy: Focused on the leak, he notices more disasters: drywall bubbling, the smell of mold.

storyboard.claim: Staying focused on the leak, I just notice more disasters: bubbling drywall, mold.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The reader afraid in the kitchen under the leak.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Back to the kitchen to show the effect of the thesis.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows noticing more disasters as the result of the focus.

explainedBy: The stressed driver wrenches the radio dial and gets nothing but static: the road scene is the radio metaphor.

storyboard.claim: I am the stressed driver wrenching the dial between stations getting only static.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The reader as an angry driver on the highway.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Switches from the kitchen to the radio metaphor.
storyboard.addedInformation: Makes the static literal: a frustrated driver.

explainedBy: The same driver stops wrestling the dial: anger turns to calm as he tunes to the music he wants.

storyboard.claim: Stop wrestling with the dial, breathe, and tune smoothly to the music you want.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The same driver, now relaxed and smiling.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same road; his face changes from angry to calm.
storyboard.addedInformation: Gives the static story its resolution.

explainedBy: Host A asks why a faked smile is exhausting; the mask icon and her forced smile show the pretending.

storyboard.claim: Why does faking a smile when deeply miserable feel so exhausting?
storyboard.concreteVisual: Host A with a forced smile beside a mask while Host B listens.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: New question that follows the tune-your-frequency idea.
storyboard.addedInformation: Introduces the fake smile as the thing being questioned (her smile is forced).

explainedBy: Host B answers: faking means fighting your internal navigation system, shown as the compass.

storyboard.claim: You are aggressively fighting your own internal navigation system.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Host B explaining beside a compass.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Answers the question of the previous beat.
storyboard.addedInformation: Introduces the compass as the inner navigation system.

explainedBy: Host A offers a picture: a heavy antique brass compass, drawn on screen.

storyboard.claim: At war with your own mechanics; imagine a heavy antique brass pocket compass.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Host A describing the compass icon.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Switches speaker to introduce the visual.
storyboard.addedInformation: Makes the metaphor object visible.

explainedBy: The same compass, but its face is a feeling scale rather than compass points.

storyboard.claim: The compass face has a feeling scale instead of north, east and west.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The same compass icon with Host A describing it.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same stage; the compass gets its meaning.
storyboard.addedInformation: States what the compass measures.

explainedBy: The compass scale: absolute despair at the bottom and relief and joy at the top.

storyboard.claim: At the top absolute relief and joy, at the bottom despair and powerlessness.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A spectrum from DESPAIR to RELIEF AND JOY.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns the described compass face into a scale.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the two ends of the feeling scale.

explainedBy: Negative emotions are a reading from an instrument, not a disease to cure or mask.

storyboard.claim: We treat negative emotions as a disease to cure or mask, not a precision instrument.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Host B with the compass behind him as the instrument.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Back to hosts with the compass as the instrument.
storyboard.addedInformation: Reframes feelings as readings.

explainedBy: The reader is still at work at 11 p.m.: the clock beside a tired person.

storyboard.claim: It is 11 p.m. and you are in a real-life situation.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The reader tired in the office with a clock.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Moves from the metaphor to real life.
storyboard.addedInformation: Sets the time of the late night grind.

explainedBy: Same office and clock: alone, staring at a spreadsheet, eyes burning.

storyboard.claim: Alone in the home office staring at a bright spreadsheet, eyes burning.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The same reader seated at the desk in the late hour.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same stage; he sits down to the work.
storyboard.addedInformation: Adds the lonely work and physical strain.

explainedBy: He mutters through gritted teeth that he has to be positive: the face is clenched.

storyboard.claim: Back aching, he mutters through gritted teeth that he must finish and be positive.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The same reader with a clenched angry face, talking.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same stage; the face tightens.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the forced positivity as a clenched jaw.

explainedBy: He says I love my job while forcing it: a smile worn like the mask.

storyboard.claim: I am a team player, I love my job: forcing toxic plastic positivity.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The reader smiling beside a mask: a false face.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same office; the smile is put on.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the smile is worn, not felt.

explainedBy: The mask stays while his body collapses: the forced smile against the exhausted nervous system.

storyboard.claim: While he forces positivity, every fiber of his nervous system screams in exhaustion.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The same reader slumped and sad beside the mask.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same stage; the smile drops, the exhaustion shows.
storyboard.addedInformation: Contrasts the false face with the real feeling.

explainedBy: Host B reads the compass for the late-night worker: exhaustion is a reading, not a weakness.

storyboard.claim: Exhaustion and resentment are not random misfires or a sign of weakness.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Host B explaining beside the compass.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Back to the hosts to interpret the late night.
storyboard.addedInformation: Rereads the feeling as a signal.

explainedBy: The compass gauges your relationship with your inner being.

storyboard.claim: Emotions are a physical indication of your relationship with your inner being.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The same hosts and compass.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same stage; the compass gets its reference.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names what the feelings point to.

explainedBy: Host A asks for a definition; the asker and the explainer are the relationship.

storyboard.claim: That sounds esoteric; what does inner being actually mean here?
storyboard.concreteVisual: Host A asking, Host B listening.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Host A challenges the new term.
storyboard.addedInformation: Asks for a plain definition.

noVisual: a broader non-physical part of you has no icon in the vocabulary
explainedBy: Host B defines inner being as the broader non-physical part of you; only text can carry it.

storyboard.claim: Your inner being is the broader non-physical part of you.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Host B answering Host A.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Answers the question of the previous beat.
storyboard.addedInformation: Gives the definition (text-led: no icon draws it).

explainedBy: At the desk he forces a smile while feeling miserable: the mask worn over his real face.

storyboard.claim: Forcing a smile at the desk while internally feeling miserable.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The reader smiling with a mask beside him.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Moves from the definition to the desk example.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the faked happiness the definition is applied to.

explainedBy: The forced smile puts the conscious thought out of alignment with the inner being.

storyboard.claim: Conscious thought is out of alignment with your inner being.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A flow from FORCED SMILE to OUT OF ALIGNMENT.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns the desk example into a cause and effect.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the misalignment as the effect.

explainedBy: The same chain grows one step: the exhaustion comes from the friction of that misalignment.

storyboard.claim: Exhaustion comes from the energetic friction of the misalignment.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The same flow with ENERGETIC FRICTION added.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Adds one label to the chain.
storyboard.addedInformation: Says where the tiredness comes from.

explainedBy: Despite all the labels, there are only two emotions, sorted into feels good and feels bad.

storyboard.claim: Fundamentally there are really only two emotions.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A sorter with FEELS GOOD and FEELS BAD.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Moves to the emotional guidance system.
storyboard.addedInformation: Reduces every emotion to two.

explainedBy: When it feels good the compass points true: joy or relief means alignment.

storyboard.claim: Joy, eagerness, even a sigh of relief means the compass is pointing true.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Both hosts smiling beside the compass.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Takes the good side of the two emotions.
storyboard.addedInformation: Makes feeling good a reading of alignment.

explainedBy: The thought matches the inner being: the same compass reading.

storyboard.claim: Your current thought is in perfect alignment with your broader inner being.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The same hosts and compass.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same stage; states what the true reading means.
storyboard.addedInformation: Says what the good feeling confirms.

noVisual: no icon for an alarm bell or for anger, fear and guilt as signals
explainedBy: The bad emotions are shown in a person: an angry reader shows the alarm sounding.

storyboard.claim: When you feel anger, fear, guilt or resentment, it is a literal alarm bell.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The reader angry in the kitchen.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns to the bad side of the two emotions.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the negative emotions (face and text only).

noVisual: no icon reads as an alarm bell or as data
explainedBy: The alarm is only information: the reader's face turns from anger to a worried reading.

storyboard.claim: It is pure data telling you that you are misaligned.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The same reader, face now worried.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same stage; the anger becomes a signal.
storyboard.addedInformation: Adds that the bad feeling is information, not a verdict.

explainedBy: Back to the compass: the bad feeling says your focus points away from what you want, so faking cannot work.

storyboard.claim: Your focus is pointing directly away from what you desire, which is why faking it does not work.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Host B with the compass.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Back to the hosts to draw the conclusion.
storyboard.addedInformation: Explains why faking fails.

explainedBy: The mask is the fake smile; his sad slumped real feeling is what the law responds to.

storyboard.claim: The law responds to the feeling in your gut, not the fake smile.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The reader sad beside a mask: the true feeling and the false face.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Returns to the desk to show the faked smile.
storyboard.addedInformation: Contrasts the gut feeling with the mask.

explainedBy: What the universe reads is the resentment behind the mask, not the words I love my job.

storyboard.claim: The universe reads the deep resentment, not the words I love my job.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The same reader, face now angry behind the mask.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same stage; the real feeling shows.
storyboard.addedInformation: Says which one the universe reads.

explainedBy: Host A pushes back on the idea, Host B invites it: asker against explainer.

storyboard.claim: A moral loophole: Host A pushes back and Host B says go for it.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Host A with a skeptical smirk, Host B waiting.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Host A raises a new objection.
storyboard.addedInformation: Opens the objection about feeling good over something terrible.
